reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added 100-repetition bootstrapped train/test splits with CI for all metrics.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: The fact that some patients were associated with multiple admissions might positively bias the performance of the model. Recommend including only the first admission per patient.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added sensitivity analysis with first-admission-only and showed consistent results.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: XGBoost has equivalent or better performance compared to transformer. XGBoost doesn't incorporate varying time-series. Why should clinicians prefer a more complex model that is harder to implement?
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added complexity-performance trade-off analysis. Recommended XGBoost for practical deployment.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: ICD codes are notoriously inaccurate — over 30% of patients in claims with acute ischemic stroke did not actually have the condition. Recommend independent audit of random sample.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added chart review validation of 200 random patients confirming >95% accuracy of ICD coding.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: The study period involves initial phases of COVID-19. Do models account for whether a patient's stroke was provoked by COVID-19?
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added COVID-19 status as covariate in sensitivity analysis.

reviewer_strengths.text: Commend the authors for using two different patient cohorts from different countries to ensure generalizability. Diverse types of data with time-variant and time-invariant information is a strength.

entries.paper_title: Methodological choices and clinical usefulness for machine learning predictions of outcome in Internet-based cognitive behavioural therapy
entries.prediction_task: Treatment outcome prediction in Internet-based CBT (80 model comparison)

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: 67% accuracy defined as benchmark for clinical usefulness. Unclear why a 33% error rate should be good enough for clinical practice. Base rate of the binary variable (50% symptom reduction yes/no) should be reported to evaluate prediction quality.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added base rate reporting and clinical justification for the 67% threshold based on existing literature.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Introduction seems superficial and does not consider relevant literature on predictive models in psychotherapy research, especially for binary outcomes. Comparable recent papers in dropout prediction not cited.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Expanded introduction with relevant psychotherapy prediction literature.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Unconvinced by multiple imputation of outcomes. Potential risk of introducing label noise. Authors should discuss this in the discussion.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added discussion of imputation risks. Results presented both with and without outcome imputation.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Great that ML pipeline is available, but code is hard to read from a PDF. Please upload to GitHub.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Code uploaded to GitHub repository.

reviewer_strengths.text: Addresses important and topical issue. Provides a guide for data analysis on adequate algorithms and methodological choices. Methodologically sound and well-written.

entries.paper_title: AI-guided patient stratification improves outcomes and efficiency in the AMARANTH Alzheimer's Disease clinical trial
entries.prediction_task: AD patient stratification for clinical trial enrichment (trained on ADNI, applied to AMARANTH trial)

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Results are not very impressive — mainly the difference between sensitivity and specificity. Existing approaches show much better performance up to 97% accuracy. Technical contributions are limited.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Clarified that the novelty is cross-dataset generalization (ADNI→AMARANTH without retraining), not raw accuracy. Added context for existing methods.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: The most critical element — that the model was trained on ADNI and applied to AMARANTH without retraining — is not sufficiently emphasised. This represents the key contribution and should be made clear earlier.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Restructured introduction and abstract to emphasize cross-dataset generalization upfront.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Since the true treatment effect in clinical trials is inherently unknown, further discussion of what evidence supports the model's consistency across datasets would strengthen the manuscript.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added discussion of external consistency evidence and limitations of post-hoc trial analysis.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Figures need axes labels and units. The outcomes and methodology are not reflecting the claim of interpretable AI model.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Improved all figure labels and added interpretability analysis section.

reviewer_strengths.text: Highly significant and original contribution. Demonstrates that ML model trained on ADNI can be applied to AMARANTH trial without retraining — going well beyond reliable insights: rescuing a clinical trial. Provides generalisable framework for precision medicine.

entries.paper_title: Multimodal deep learning for Alzheimer's disease dementia assessment
entries.prediction_task: AD dementia vs non-AD dementia vs MCI vs normal cognition classification

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: GPs usually do not have access to MRI scanner — one of the most important features is MRI-based. For clinical trials, biomarker evidence for amyloid pathology would be preferred but is not included.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added analysis of model performance without MRI and discussed deployment scenarios.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Model trained on clinical diagnosis — up to 30% of individuals with clinical AD dementia do not have AD pathology. Comparison with clinicians reflects differences between new vs old clinicians, not model superiority. Also APOE is missing for non-AD cohorts — presence of APOE alone could predict AD vs non-AD almost perfectly.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added neuropathological validation subset and discussed diagnostic label noise. APOE missingness handled with explicit analysis.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Dementia vs non-dementia classification is trivial — diagnosis determined based on neuropsych test scores and MMSE, so it's circular that these features predict the diagnosis perfectly. The harder and more relevant task is AD vs non-AD dementias.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added focused analysis on AD vs non-AD subtypes and discussed the circular nature of the dementia vs non-dementia classification.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: How were MRI scans harmonised across cohorts? How were cohort-specific missing data dealt with? APOE is missing in entire Parkinson and FTD cohorts — this creates a confound.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added MRI harmonization details and missing data handling methodology.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Unclear how external validation dataset was chosen. Manuscript mentions splitting into folds but explanation vague. How are AUC and other metrics independent of tuning and training?
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Clarified validation strategy with explicit held-out external datasets.

reviewer_strengths.text: Highly novel — combines datasets at much larger scales than previous studies with several different modalities and multiple layers of validation (technical, clinical, neuropathological).

entries.paper_title: AI-driven fusion of multimodal data for Alzheimer's disease biomarker assessment
entries.prediction_task: Amyloid and tau PET status prediction from multimodal clinical data (without PET scan)

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: AUROC of 0.79/0.84 for amyloid/tau classification — should report calibration and net benefit analysis. Without these, clinical applicability cannot be assessed.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added calibration plots and DCA analysis.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Seven cohorts used but unclear how independent the external validation truly is. Need clear delineation of which cohorts used for development vs validation.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Restructured to clearly separate 4 development cohorts from 3 validation cohorts.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: The clinical utility depends on whether this replaces PET scanning. How does the model perform in the specific clinical scenario where PET is being considered but not yet obtained?
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added analysis of model as PET pre-screening tool with cost-effectiveness comparison.

reviewer_strengths.text: Large-scale study integrating data from seven cohorts comprising 12,185 participants. Practical clinical relevance for reducing need for expensive PET scans.
